meta.description: Every constant the Foreground money engine uses. Each entry has value(s), a unit and a source. "Foreground estimate" means we could not open a public source for the value; it is our own planning assumption and must be shown as an estimate.

diningAreaShare.unit: share of total area used for seating

turnsVerdict.note: Applies to true break-even (profit zero). Turns are break-even covers per day divided by the seats the owner will operate (the smaller of the seats wanted and the seats that fit). comfortable when turns/day <= comfortableMax; stretch when <= stretchMax; otherwise unlikely. Anchor: Foundra's example counter-service restaurant does 175 covers on 50 seats (3.5 turns/day) on a normal day. Break-even needing a full normal day is the stretch limit; needing under about 60% of one is comfortable. Table-service concepts turn slower (ChowNow: about 1 hour 15 minutes per table), quick-service and cafes faster. The limits themselves are ours.

Los Angeles.note: No public per-SF Los Angeles figure could be opened. Ask the landlord for the actual NNN schedule.

Houston.note: Used only when the listing quotes no rent.

Los Angeles.note: Used only when the listing quotes no rent.

hood.note: Exhaust hood install or modification including ductwork, fire suppression and roof penetration.

greasePointOfUse.note: Lower part of Block Renovation's $5,000-25,000 grease interceptor range; the split between point-of-use and in-ground is ours.

greaseInGround.note: Exterior in-ground interceptor including excavation. Block Renovation gives $5,000-25,000 for interceptors overall.

source.label: Projul restaurant and bar build-out guide

adaRestroom.note: Single ADA restroom retrofit. Path-of-travel work can add more.

source.label: Pulse RevOps, ADA restroom and path-of-travel cost in a buildout

sewer.note: Connection or capacity fees vary widely by city.

secondGen.note: Refresh of a former restaurant (finishes, layout tweaks, repairs) with kitchen systems, FF&E and permits priced as separate X-Ray lines. No public source could be opened for a refresh-only rate. Published all-in second-generation figures are higher because they include equipment and systems: $73/SF survey median (RestaurantOwner.com 2018 via UpMenu), $150-300/SF (NineGuides).

shell.note: First-generation shell, or a space with no sign of a past restaurant. Low: RestaurantOwner.com 2018 survey median for new construction ($193/SF; converting a non-restaurant space was $146/SF). High: low end of NineGuides' $300-600/SF shell range. Kitchen systems are priced as separate X-Ray lines.

secondGen.note: Former restaurant, kitchen fixtures largely in place: mostly furniture, fixtures and decor. Derived from Foundra's $10,000-50,000 for furniture, fixtures and decor spread over a 40-seat room; the per-seat conversion is ours.

shell.note: Full kitchen equipment plus furniture. Derived from Foundra's $20,000-100,000 kitchen equipment plus $10,000-50,000 furniture, fixtures and decor spread over a 40-seat room; the per-seat conversion is ours.

layout.note: Used by the Layout Studio (lib/layout). Costs are added on top of the X-Ray when the drawn plan asks for them. No public per-unit source could be opened for these; they are planning assumptions and are shown as estimates.

barCounterPerM.note: About $400-1,000 per linear foot for a plumbed bar with millwork, sinks and a back bar.

serviceCounterPerM.note: About $200-500 per linear foot for an order or pickup counter.

extraRestroom.unit: USD per restroom beyond the first
extraRestroom.note: A new plumbed, accessible restroom room. The first restroom is priced by the X-Ray ADA restroom line.

hoodRelocation.note: Moving an existing cook line means a new roof penetration, duct run and fire-suppression re-pipe.

kitchenPlumbingReroute.note: Gas, floor drains and grease waste rerouted to a moved cook line.

extraWalkIn.unit: USD per walk-in beyond the first
extraWalkIn.note: Same range as the X-Ray walk-in line.

patioSetup.note: Sidewalk or patio permit, barriers and outdoor-rated furniture. Needs the landlord's and the city's consent.

relocationToleranceM.unit: metres a cook line can shift under the same hood before it counts as moved

aisleM.unit: metres, main aisle between table rows

dwellMinutes.unit: minutes a guest holds a seat
dwellMinutes.note: Used only by the day simulator. Table service about 1 hour 15 minutes per table (ChowNow); the others are ours.

serviceDay.unit: open hour, close hour, and the hours demand peaks
serviceDay.note: Used only by the day simulator: a lunch peak and a dinner peak; guests who wait longer than patienceMinutes leave.

maybeShare.unit: share of an unknown (maybe) line counted in the total

contingency.note: Foundra: budget for costs 30% higher than planned.

secondGenWithHood.note: Renovation of an existing restaurant space: 3-6 months.

secondGen.note: Second-generation space without a confirmed hood: between the renovation and new-construction ranges.

year1Ramp.unit: share of steady-state sales reached in year 1
year1Ramp.note: Foundra: 6-18 months to reach profitability. Years 2 and 3 run at steady state.

failure.unit: share of independent full-service startups failing in year 1; years

source.label: Luo & Stark 2014, Only the Bad Die Young: Restaurant Mortality in the Western US

feasibility.note: Used by lib/feasibility (Imagine mode). Code facts cite the model code; Houston and Los Angeles adopt amended editions, so the local section number can differ. Dollar ranges and timelines are planning ranges from our research, not quotes; where no public source could be opened they are marked Foreground estimate and must be shown as estimates.

typeI.note: New Type I hood with listed grease duct to the roof, exhaust and make-up air fans, and a wet-chemical suppression system. Long duct runs, rated shafts through an upper floor, or pollution-control units push it past the high end.

relocate.note: Moving an existing hood: new roof penetration, duct run and suppression re-pipe. Same range as layout.hoodRelocation.

recertify.note: Hood cleaning, suppression inspection and tag, and an air-balance check when a new operator takes over an existing hood.

clearanceIn.note: IMC 507.2.6 (hood) and 506.3.6 (grease duct). Listed reduced-clearance wraps can lower it.

code.text: Type I hood required over appliances that produce grease or smoke
Grease duct: welded steel, 18 in clearance to combustibles, discharge above the roof
Hood, duct and suppression system installed and inspected as one system

source.label: NFPA 96, ventilation control and fire protection of commercial cooking operations

underSink.note: Hydromechanical (point-of-use) interceptor at the sinks, installed.

inGround.note: Gravity interceptor (750-1,500 gal) outside in the ground: excavation, tank, vents, sampling well, paving repair.

code.text: Grease interceptor required on food-service drains; sized by flow and placed where it can be cleaned

source.label: 2021 International Plumbing Code, chapter 10 (traps, interceptors and separators)

nonBearing.unit: USD per opening up to 10 ft
nonBearing.note: Partition demolition, patching floor and ceiling, rerouting the wiring inside it.

bearing.unit: USD per opening up to 10 ft
bearing.note: Shoring, steel or engineered beam, posts and footings. Wider openings and exterior walls cost more.

engineer.note: Structural engineer's site visit, calculations and stamped drawing for the permit.

code.text: An alteration must not reduce the structure's capacity; structural changes need stamped drawings

minHeightFt.note: IBC 1208.2: occupiable spaces need a ceiling of at least 7 ft 6 in.

sfPerSprinklerHead.note: NFPA 13 ordinary-hazard spacing; one head per 130 SF is the planning count.

sprinklerHeadRelocation.note: Drop or relocate a head to the new ceiling plane, including the fire-sprinkler permit share.

ductAndDiffusers.note: Extending supply drops, diffusers, returns and lights down to a lower ceiling.

code.text: Minimum ceiling height 7 ft 6 in
Sprinkler heads must sit at the new ceiling; a deep space above it may need heads too
Keep 18 in between the hood or grease duct and combustible ceiling framing

trenchPerFt.note: Saw-cut the slab, trench, lay drain and vent, backfill and patch.

slabScan.note: Ground-penetrating radar scan before cutting; a post-tensioned slab cannot be trenched freely.

defaultRunFt.note: Assumed run to the nearest drain when the distance is not known.

code.text: New drains need slope, venting and an inspection before the slab is closed

waterClosetPer.unit: occupants per water closet, each sex (restaurants)
waterClosetPer.note: IPC Table 403.1, assembly A-2 restaurants: 1 per 75 male and 1 per 75 female; lavatories 1 per 200.

singleRoomMaxLoad.note: IPC 403.2: separate facilities are not required at 15 occupants or fewer.

newRestroom.note: A new plumbed accessible single-user room. Same range as layout.extraRestroom.

source.label: Pulse RevOps, ADA restroom and path-of-travel cost in a buildout

pathOfTravelShare.note: Path-of-travel upgrades are required up to 20% of the cost of altering a primary function area.

code.text: Fixture counts by occupant load: one water closet per 75 of each sex in a restaurant
Accessible restroom, door clearances and route
Path of travel: up to 20% of the alteration cost goes to the route, restrooms and entrance

diningNetSfPerPerson.note: IBC Table 1004.5, assembly without fixed seats, tables and chairs.

2021 International Building Code, chapter 10 (means of egress)

sprinklerLoad.note: IBC 903.2.1.2: an A-2 fire area with 100 or more occupants (or over 5,000 SF) must be sprinklered.

storefrontPerFt.unit: USD per linear ft of storefront

barPerFt.unit: USD per linear ft of bar
barPerFt.note: Plumbed bar with millwork, sinks and a back bar. Same as layout.barCounterPerM.
